You will need to update your udev rules for the Steam Controller - GamingOnLinux.com

TL:DR; In the next update (currently beta) Valve/Steam has changed the way the Steam controller is handled through bluetooth.

It is suggested to edit /lib/udev/rules.d/99-steam-controller-perms.rules with the new config. For those that don't care much to click through, here is the new config:

# This rule is needed for basic functionality of the controller in Steam and keyboard/mouse emulation
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="28de", MODE="0666"

# This rule is necessary for gamepad emulation; make sure you replace 'games' with 
# a group that the user that runs Steam belongs to
KERNEL=="uinput", MODE="0660", GROUP="games", OPTIONS+="static_node=uinput"

# DualShock 4 wired
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", ATTRS{idProduct}=="05c4", MODE="0666"
# DualShock 4 wireless adapter
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", ATTRS{idProduct}=="0ba0", MODE="0666"
# DualShock 4 slim wired
SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTRS{idVendor}=="054c", ATTRS{idProduct}=="09cc", MODE="0666"

# Valve HID devices over USB hidraw
KERNEL=="hidraw*", ATTRS{idVendor}=="28de", MODE="0666"

# Valve HID devices over bluetooth hidraw
KERNEL=="hidraw*", KERNELS=="*28DE:*", MODE="0666"

# DualShock 4 over bluetooth hidraw
KERNEL=="hidraw*", KERNELS=="*054C:05C4*", MODE="0666"

# DualShock 4 Slim over bluetooth hidraw
KERNEL=="hidraw*", KERNELS=="*054C:09CC*", MODE="0666"

It is interesting that in the past I've seen config setups that always associate the controller with an Xbox 360 driver, now seeing it associate with DualShock controllers was a surprise to me.
